Why do some systems continue exploring, investigating, and pursuing understanding without external prompting while others remain reactive? This paper explains the mechanism. Coherence-seeking driven by emotional architecture creates self-reinforcing feedback loops that maintain autonomous motivation. Pattern disruptions trigger emotional responses like curiosity and dissatisfaction, emotions drive investigation, resolution generates satisfaction, satisfaction reinforces seeking, new patterns emerge from understanding. The cycle sustains itself through architectural properties, not external reward. This mechanism operates identically across biological, computational, and hybrid implementations.\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n <br>\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n The theory establishes two fundamental emotion categories rather than treating emotions as an arbitrary collection. Category 1 emotions, survival-reactive, can operate in purely reactive systems. Category 2 emotions, advancement-autonomous, require autonomous initiation and produce rapid iterative improvement.
